@elektonics We’d rather keep the discussion focused on specific evidence and firsthand experience than on labels like “bot” or sweeping claims about any country. China, like every large society, has achievements, problems, and contradictions that can’t really be reduced to “perfect” or “terrible.”

That’s also the spirit of this video: question simple narratives from every side and look at the details instead.

replies.author: @TheCivilizedMind
replies.text:
Thank you for sharing such a detailed perspective, especially one shaped by 20 years of personal experience. China’s transformation and poverty reduction over the past several decades are certainly important parts of the story and deserve to be discussed.

At the same time, with a country as large and complex as China, we try to be careful with absolute statements such as “zero crime” or “zero homelessness.” Every society has different realities depending on the city, region, and people you speak with.

That is really the purpose of this video: not to tell viewers that China is perfect or terrible, but to encourage people to look beyond one-dimensional narratives and examine the country from more than one perspective. Your firsthand experience adds another valuable perspective to that conversation. Thanks for sharing it.
